summary: Wooden Ringwood Company lookout in Ringwood State Park, destroyed by fire in 1954; registered 2014; no source describes the site today.

facts.design: Wooden lookout, probably no more than 40 ft tall (register estimate)
facts.status_note: Destroyed by fire in 1954 according to the register; no source describes what remains at the site
facts.agency: New Jersey Division of Parks & Forestry

access.note: Site lies inside Ringwood State Park; no source says whether the old site or its trail is open or marked

visit.trail_note: Register says a trail once led from Camp Yawpo to the lookout; no source says whether it can still be followed

events.note: Destroyed by a fire, according to Section 2 Chief Fire Warden Frank Scardo (register description)
Registered April 16, 2014 as US 1550, NJ 2; nominated by Bob Spear

evidence.supports: one of several lookouts erected by the Ringwood Company to protect woodland from wildfire
evidence.quote: This wooden lookout was one of several erected by the Ringwood Company to protect their woodland holdings from wildfire.

evidence.supports: probably no more than 40 ft tall; operated by local resident Ralph Colfax
evidence.quote: Probably no more than 40' tall, it was operated by local resident Ralph Colfax.

evidence.supports: destroyed in 1954 by a fire, per Section 2 Chief Fire Warden Frank Scardo
evidence.quote: It was destroyed in 1954 by a fire according to Section 2 Chief Fire Warden Frank Scardo.

evidence.supports: no known road access; a trail once led from Camp Yawpo to the lookout
evidence.quote: There was no known road access to the site, but a trail led from Camp Yawpo to the lookout.

evidence.supports: registered April 16, 2014 as US 1550, NJ 2; nominated by Bob Spear
administered by New Jersey Division of Parks & Forestry

notes_for_editor: Built date and builder are not given by any source read, so no build event is recorded. The only account of the 1954 fire is the register's own description; no newspaper or state record was found. Ralph Colfax and Frank Scardo appear only in the register. Brief's 'removed 1954' matches the register's Removed field. Story says no source describes the site today.
